value.text: This computer most likely has a faster graphics card (NVIDIA or AMD), as laptops with 165 Hz screens do. The browser draws on the integrated graphics chip (Intel(R) UHD Graphics) and leaves that card unused. On it: more detail, full resolution, more frames per second. Switch the browser to it:Fastest, in the browser: open this address in a new tab, choose Enabled, then press Relaunch: chrome://flags/#force-high-performance-gpu Copy the addressIn Windows: open the graphics settings (Settings, System, Display, Graphics), add this browser to the list if it is not there, choose High performance for it, then close the browser completely and start it again. If nothing changes, restart the computer. Open Windows graphics settingsThe faster card uses more power: on battery the laptop runs for a shorter time and gets warmer. To undo, choose Disabled again in the browser, or in Windows the option that lets Windows decide.Got itDo not show again

softNote.text: The browser is drawing this page in software (SwiftShader): on the processor, not on a graphics card, so everything here runs very slowly. This usually has one of two causes:Graphics acceleration may be switched off in the browser. Open this address in a new tab, switch graphics (hardware) acceleration on, and restart the browser: chrome://settings/system Copy the addressThe graphics driver may be disabled or missing, so the browser has no graphics card to draw on.In Windows open Device Manager, Display adapters: every adapter must be enabled and have a driver installed. On a laptop a disabled integrated chip (Intel) can leave the browser with no graphics card at all, even when there is an NVIDIA card: enable the Intel adapter again.Got itDo not show again
